title: SAP Sales Order Cross-Application Map
purpose: Separate the business process from the system that originates the order and the application that executes the next responsibility.
memory_rule: A sales order has three different questions: who created it, what business branch it represents, and which application owns the next decision.

code_system.ORC.SD.<MNEMONIC>: upstream origin or orchestrator that creates or governs a sales order
code_system.INT.SD.<MNEMONIC>: cross-application execution or control handoff from Sales
code_system.EVT.SD.<MNEMONIC>: event-driven integration contract around the Sales business object

center.rule: Keep Sales Order as the commercial execution anchor. Origin and downstream ownership are modeled as separate edges, not baked into the process name.

origins.title: External App via Sales Order API
origins.memory_hook: An external app creates the order; S/4HANA still owns sales-order semantics.
constraints: Choose V4/V2 by required feature support, not by fashion.
Do not duplicate pricing or ATP logic in the caller unless that is an explicit architecture decision.

origins.title: External Web Shop / Landscape via A2A Bulk
origins.memory_hook: Reliable asynchronous order capture when the sender and S/4HANA do not need to share one UI transaction.
constraints: Exactly-once style processing requires disciplined message identifiers.
A technical receipt is not the same as a successfully created business order.

origins.title: External Buyer / EDI-style B2B
origins.memory_hook: The buyer sends a purchase order; the supplier system turns it into a sales order and answers with business documents.
constraints: If the buyer uses IDoc/EDI formats, mapping belongs in the integration layer rather than hidden SD exits.
The document chain is bidirectional; order creation alone is not the integration.

origins.title: SAP Commerce Cloud Order Management
origins.memory_hook: The storefront asks S/4HANA for the real commercial answer before or while it creates the order.
constraints: The Commerce integration has feature differences between API versions.
Product-variant scenarios need separate configuration integration choices.

origins.title: SAP CPQ Quote to Sales Order
origins.memory_hook: Configure and negotiate upstream, then simulate and create the executable order in S/4HANA.
constraints: Header-level CPQ discounts have documented limitations in this integration pattern.
Keep the quote/order reference so support can trace commercial origin.

origins.title: SAP Sales Cloud v2 Opportunity-to-Order
origins.memory_hook: Pipeline and customer engagement live in Sales Cloud; fulfillment contract lands in S/4HANA.
constraints: CRM opportunity ownership and ERP order ownership are different responsibilities.
Mapping governance matters more than another custom field copied everywhere.

origins.title: Solution Order Orchestration
origins.memory_hook: One commercial package can release physical sales, service, subscription and project follow-up objects.
flow: Sales Order / Service / Subscription / Project Follow-Up
constraints: Do not treat Solution Order as a fancy sales-order type; it orchestrates different business objects.
Failure handling must show which follow-up transaction failed.

origins.title: Subscription Delivery Plan to Sales Order
origins.memory_hook: The long-lived contract schedules recurring physical demand; generated sales orders execute each cycle.
constraints: Already processed plan lines are not rewritten by later contract changes.
Separate lifecycle ownership from generated order fulfillment.

origins.title: Customer Project to Sales Order Context
origins.memory_hook: Project stage and contract model govern the sales order used to bill project work.
constraints: Allowed API operations can depend on project stage.
Project services need project billing logic, not stock-delivery assumptions.

handoffs.title: Production Planning / Manufacturing
handoffs.owns_next: planning, components, production execution and manufacturing dates
handoffs.failure_signal: sales order exists but supply object or feasible production date is missing

handoffs.title: Project / EPPM
handoffs.trigger: customer fulfillment is project- or WBS-driven
handoffs.owns_next: project structure, project stock or project service execution, cost collection
handoffs.failure_signal: sales contract and project execution are no longer aligned

handoffs.title: Sourcing & Procurement
handoffs.owns_next: supplier sourcing, purchasing confirmation, receipt/invoice evidence
handoffs.failure_signal: SD looks correct but procurement document or supplier evidence is missing

handoffs.title: Extended Warehouse Management
handoffs.trigger: delivery or return requires warehouse execution
handoffs.owns_next: warehouse tasks, picking, packing, receiving and warehouse inspection where configured
handoffs.failure_signal: commercial document is ready but warehouse execution/status is not

handoffs.title: Transportation Management
handoffs.trigger: sales order / scheduling agreement is transportation relevant
handoffs.failure_signal: delivery promise exists but transportation demand or execution is missing

handoffs.title: SAP GTS / Trade Compliance
handoffs.trigger: sales document requires external compliance check
handoffs.via: legal control, embargo and screening status
handoffs.failure_signal: order is commercially valid but blocked for legal or compliance reasons

handoffs.title: SAP Credit Management
handoffs.trigger: credit-relevant order/customer value must be checked
handoffs.owns_next: risk evaluation, documented credit decision and release
handoffs.failure_signal: order is valid but downstream processing is blocked by credit result

handoffs.title: Finance / Revenue & Receivables
handoffs.trigger: billing, PGI or revenue-recognition event occurs
handoffs.owns_next: receivable, revenue, COGS, margin, revenue recognition
handoffs.failure_signal: logistics completed but financial document or recognition state is wrong

handoffs.title: Service / Solution Business
handoffs.trigger: sale includes service, repair, subscription or mixed solution scope
handoffs.via: solution order / service order / repair / subscription follow-up
handoffs.owns_next: service execution, service contract or subscription lifecycle
handoffs.failure_signal: sales-side reference exists but service-side follow-up was not distributed

eventing.title: Sales Order Business Events
eventing.pattern: Publish the business event; let Event Mesh or another broker route it to side-by-side consumers. Fetch detail through an API if the event payload is intentionally small.
not_for: replacing synchronous pricing/ATP when the caller needs an answer before order confirmation

lead_checks: Is this genuinely a new business process, or only a new order origin?
Who is the system of record for price, ATP, credit and configuration at the moment of promise?
Which downstream application owns the next irreversible decision?
What correlation key lets support trace the process across systems?
Which integration is synchronous because the customer waits, and which should be asynchronous because the process can continue later?
